title: The Apprentice and the Perfectionist
script: Zaid: [frustrated] I've rewritten the introduction eleven times now, and it still reads like I'm apologizing for having written it at all.
Mentor: [gently] Eleven times is a suspiciously precise number for someone who claims not to be counting.
Zaid: [defensive] I'm not obsessive about it. I simply refuse to submit something mediocre when I know it's capable of being better.
Mentor: [wry] A noble sentiment that has, in my experience, ruined more brilliant careers than mediocrity ever managed to.
Zaid: [surprised] That seems a rather generous defense of mediocrity, for someone who's published as extensively as you have.
Mentor: [amused] I'm not defending mediocrity. I'm questioning your premise that the twelfth draft is meaningfully closer to some Platonic ideal than the fourth was.
Zaid: [considering] It has to be, surely. Each revision addresses something the last one missed.

Mentor: [measured] Or each revision addresses something increasingly trivial, because you've already resolved the substantive problems and are now merely rearranging furniture to avoid the discomfort of finishing.
Mentor: [understanding] Perfectionism disguises itself so convincingly as diligence that even the perfectionist rarely catches the substitution happening.
Zaid: [candid] So what's the alternative, submitting work I know is flawed?
Mentor: [firm] All work is flawed, Zaid, including whatever you eventually publish after your hundredth revision. The only genuine choice is which flaws you're willing to stand behind publicly.
Zaid: [thoughtful] That reframes it considerably. I've been treating flawlessness as achievable rather than as a mirage that recedes with every step toward it.
Mentor: [warmly] Precisely. Send me draft eleven by Friday, flaws included, and I promise the sky will not fall.
Zaid: [wry] And if it does fall, I suppose we'll simply revise the apocalypse a twelfth time.
Mentor: [laughing] Now you're finally getting somewhere.

Nothing at all, since revisions are random
